questions.q: Which ancient Greek idea describes the human craving for dignity and recognition?
a: Thymos, the part of the soul seeking worth
Logos, the rational ordering of the world
Eros, the drive toward beauty and union
Pathos, the emotion that overwhelms reason
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that Socrates called this longing for positive judgment thymos.

questions.q: Why did gay couples keep fighting for marriage after civil unions gave them equal legal rights?
a: They wanted the same dignity and status as heterosexual marriage
Civil unions did not grant them any economic advantages
They wanted the government to recognize religious ceremonies
Civil unions were only available in a few states at the time
questions.why: The summary frames the fight as a demand for recognition, not just for legal benefits.

questions.q: What does Fukuyama say identity politics has done to the political left?
a: Splintered it into groups too small to pursue broad equality
United its factions behind a shared economic program
Turned it into the main defender of national identity
Helped it win back working-class voters across the West
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the left is split into competing groups, which stops it addressing the broader causes of inequality.

questions.q: What kind of identity does Fukuyama think can reduce polarization?
a: A more inclusive national identity built on shared values
A stricter identity based on race, gender or religion
A purely economic identity that ignores culture
A global identity that replaces national citizenship
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues for shared belief in a country's morals, political system and commitment to human rights.

questions.q: Which recommendation for strengthening national identity does the summary mention?
a: Requiring a year or two of national service
Limiting immigration to a small annual quota
Making religious instruction mandatory in schools
Abolishing all forms of patriotic education
questions.why: The summary lists national service, secular schools, immigrant integration and welcoming newcomers as ways to build unity.
